title: X OAuth 1.0a consumer secret as a signing key, a bare 43- or 50-character value, or an oauth_consumer_secret field
summary: A signing key written as a consumer secret followed by an ampersand, a bare 43-character alphanumeric value, a bare 50-character alphanumeric value, and an oauth_consumer_secret form field.
rationale: X documents no text field or header that carries the consumer secret on the wire: it is the input of the signing key (the percent-encoded consumer secret followed by an ampersand when the token secret is not yet known), so no carrier is named for a positive (claim signing-key-input-signature-output). Lengths conflict: the provider's 2011-dated worked example uses 43 characters and describes the example only (worked-example-lengths), two artifacts capture 50 (length-50-consistency), and one artifact captures 35 to 44 with a generic pattern (length-35-to-44-single-artifact); no union is recorded (artifacts-disagree-on-secret-length, unresolved). A bare value of the consumer secret and of the token secret cannot be told apart by shape (token-secret-boundary), and whether an issued secret can contain a percent-changing character is open (percent-containing-forms). The handoff for this row says not to author a shape-only expectation. No outcome is asserted.

expectation.rationale: No outcome is asserted. Whether a signing-key text, a bare 43- or 50-character value, or an oauth_consumer_secret field carries an X OAuth 1.0a consumer secret is not stated by any X page. Settled by an X statement of key and secret lengths and when they changed, a dated archive snapshot of an X page that states one, or an X page naming a carrier.

sources.supports: In this case, the signing key should consist of the percent encoded consumer secret followed by an ampersand character ‘&’.
Rule twitter-api-secret captures 50 alphanumeric characters after a twitter keyword; rule twitter-api-key captures 25.
The consumer key detector captures 25 alphanumeric characters as the key and 50 as the secret.
Rule np.twitter.2 (Twitter Secret Key) captures 35 to 44 alphanumeric characters; rule np.twitter.1 captures 18 to 25 for the identifier.
Worked example consumer secret in the signature page (43 characters; value not copied).
